text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- French President Jacques Chirac begins a busy two-day visit to Budapest today. @

- Opposition parties told separate press conferences that a report on the Socialists' media strategy for the elections, published in Uj Magyarorszag, is consistent with reality. Socialist Party presidium member Sandor Csintalan said his party should consider reporting the matter of the document to the police.
- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny said that the period of consultations and social debates related to pension reform has been extended by one month. @
- The Socialist Party parliamentary group leader announced that if necessary, the group will pass the amendment to the privatisation law sent back by the President.

- Premier Horn told former privatisation minister Tamas Suchman that he could take the vacant post of deputy chairman of Parliament's European Integration Committee if the Socialist Party's parliamentary group unanimously backs the plan.
- The State Audit Office is expected to launch an investigation of K&H Bank, thus probably postponing its impending privatisation somewhat. @
- The information technologhy companies Optotrans and Rolitron will merge soon and became the first IT company listed on the stock exchange sometimes in the first half of this year.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Christian Democrats and the Smallholders will start joint preparations towards closer co-operation for the next parliamentary elections, said Smallholders vice-president Agnes Maczo Nagy.
- The vehicle manufacturer Raba celebrated its 100th anniversary with a HUF 1 billion pre-tax profit last year.
VILAGGAZDASAG @

- Anthony Nelson, British State Secretary for Trade, is due to arrive in Budapest today to attend the campaign Open for Business in Central Europe, aimed at promoting British trade and investments in the region.
- Hungarian shares offer the most attractive price/earnings ratio this year, according to the latest report by the investment bank Merrill Lynch.
- The Hungarian subsidiaries of the pharmaceutical company Sandoz and the chemical firm Ciba-Geigy will merge shortly, following the merger of their parent companies to form Novartis. @
- Industrial production was 1 percent below that of the previous month in November, says the Central Statistics Office.
- The vehicle manufacturer Raba celebrated its 100th anniversary with a HUF 1 billion pre-tax profit last year.
- The number of subscribers of the mobile phone company Pannon GSM increased by 100,000 to 170,000 last year.
- The foreign winners of a 1993 tender for the concessionary right to search for oil and gas in Hungary will begin exploration this spring.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @
- From January 16, the BUX Index will no longer include Goldsun in its share basket. The company is under liquidation.
- Police seized 37,000 illegitimate customs seals and HUF 500,000 worth of meal tickets in a 19th district car park.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- The Budakeszi branch of OTP Bank was robbed for the second time in two month yesterday afternoon when two men got away with about HUF 6 million.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
